sections.title: Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

questions.q: Starch digestion begins in the —
The enzyme in pancreatic juice that digests fats is —
Bile is produced by the —
The end products of protein digestion are —
Villi help in —

sections.passage: In the human body food is digested step by step. Saliva begins the digestion of starch in the mouth. In the stomach, hydrochloric acid and pepsin act on proteins. In the small intestine, bile from the liver breaks fats into tiny droplets, and pancreatic juice supplies trypsin, amylase and lipase. Digestion is completed here, and the finger-like villi absorb the products into the blood. The large intestine absorbs water from the undigested food.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Define the terms (i) osmoregulation and (ii) dialysis.
questions.answer: (i) Osmoregulation is the maintenance of the correct amount of water and mineral ions in the blood and body. (ii) Dialysis is the removal of waste from the blood of a person whose kidneys have failed, using an artificial kidney in which blood flows past a membrane bathed in dialysis fluid.

questions.q: Name two deficiency diseases caused by protein-energy malnutrition. State the symptoms of any one.
questions.answer: Marasmus and kwashiorkor. Marasmus (infants deprived of mother's milk): wasting of muscles, loose folds of skin, prominent ribs, slow growth. (Kwashiorkor: swelling, enlarged liver, dark scaly skin, reddish-brown hair, thin legs, retarded growth.)

questions.q: Why is hypertension considered a disorder of the circulatory system? Write any two of its symptoms.
questions.answer: Hypertension is high blood pressure — blood pushes too hard against the walls of the arteries, straining the heart and blood vessels. Symptoms: headache, dizziness, fatigue.

questions.q: Why are we advised to chew our food well?
questions.answer: Chewing breaks food into small pieces and mixes it with saliva, whose amylase starts digesting starch; the moist, small pieces are easy to swallow and give enzymes a larger surface to act on in the stomach and intestine.

questions.q: Why does the trachea not collapse during exhalation?
questions.answer: The trachea is supported by rings of cartilage, which keep it open even when there is little air in it.

questions.q: What is the difference between breathing and respiration?
questions.answer: Breathing is the physical process of taking in air and giving out carbon dioxide (exchange of gases in the lungs). Respiration is the oxidation of food (glucose) in the cells to release energy, with production of carbon dioxide and water.

questions.q: Classify living organisms on the basis of their mode of nutrition.
questions.answer: Autotrophs make their own food by photosynthesis (green plants, algae). Heterotrophs depend on others: holozoic (Amoeba, humans), parasitic (head louse, Cuscuta) and saprotrophic (mushroom, yeast).

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: A patient's kidneys stop working properly. Explain how dialysis helps in such a situation and why it is important.
questions.answer: In dialysis a tube from an artery takes the patient's blood to an artificial kidney. The blood flows through a tube with a thin membrane surrounded by dialysis fluid; urea and other wastes diffuse out of the blood into the fluid, while blood cells and proteins stay in. The cleaned blood is returned to a vein. It is important because without it nitrogenous wastes and excess water and salts would accumulate in the blood and poison the body; it keeps the patient alive until a kidney transplant.

questions.q: Describe the processes of transport of water and of food in plants.
questions.answer: Water and minerals absorbed by root hairs move up through the xylem (tracheids and vessels) to the leaves; this ascent of sap is driven by transpiration pull — water evaporating from the stomata pulls the water column up. Food (sugar) made in the leaves is carried by the sieve tubes of the phloem to other parts of the plant (translocation) and stored in roots, stems or fruits.

questions.q: What is meant by a balanced diet? What are its main constituents? Why should raw vegetables and fruits be regular components of meals?
questions.answer: A balanced diet contains all the essential nutrients in the right amounts and proportion for a person's age, sex and work. Constituents: carbohydrates, fats, proteins, vitamins, minerals, water and roughage. Raw vegetables and fruits supply vitamins and minerals and give roughage (fibre) that helps bowel movement and prevents constipation.

questions.q: What are enzymes? List three pancreatic enzymes and state their functions.
questions.answer: Enzymes are biological catalysts, mostly proteins, that speed up chemical reactions in the body without being used up. Pancreatic enzymes: trypsin — digests proteins (peptones to peptides); amylase — digests starch into maltose; lipase — digests fats into fatty acids and glycerol.

questions.q: Explain the mechanism of breathing in humans.
questions.answer: Inhalation: the diaphragm contracts and flattens and the rib muscles lift the ribs up and out; the chest cavity enlarges, the pressure inside falls and air rushes into the lungs. Exhalation: the diaphragm relaxes and arches up, the ribs move down and in; the chest cavity becomes smaller, the pressure rises and air is pushed out through the trachea and nose.

questions.q: Draw a diagram of the human respiratory system and label the glottis, trachea, lungs and bronchioles.
questions.answer: Diagram: nostrils → nasal cavity → pharynx; the glottis is the opening of the pharynx into the larynx/trachea; the trachea (with cartilage rings) runs down the neck and divides into two bronchi entering the two lungs; inside the lungs the bronchi branch into fine bronchioles ending in alveoli; the diaphragm lies below the lungs.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: What is photosynthesis? Explain the raw materials required for photosynthesis and how plants obtain them.
questions.answer: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants make glucose from carbon dioxide and water in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll, releasing oxygen: 6CO2 + 12H2O → C6H12O6 + 6H2O + 6O2. Raw materials: (1) carbon dioxide — taken from the air through the stomata of leaves; (2) water — absorbed from the soil by root hairs and carried up the xylem to the leaves; (3) sunlight — the source of energy, absorbed by the leaves; (4) chlorophyll — the green pigment in the chloroplasts of leaf cells, which traps light energy. The glucose formed is used or stored as starch and oxygen is released through the stomata.

questions.q: Explain the digestion of carbohydrates, proteins and fats in human beings.
questions.answer: Carbohydrates: in the mouth salivary amylase converts starch into sugar; in the small intestine pancreatic amylase changes starch to maltose and digestion is completed to glucose. Proteins: in the stomach, hydrochloric acid activates pepsin, which breaks proteins into peptones; in the small intestine trypsin of pancreatic juice breaks them further, and they are finally digested into amino acids. Fats: in the small intestine bile from the liver emulsifies fats into droplets and gives an alkaline medium; lipase of pancreatic juice changes them into fatty acids and glycerol. The end products are absorbed by the villi into the blood.
questions.note: April 2019 asked: what are enzymes, which enzymes digest nutrients, their sources in the digestive system and the function of each.

questions.q: (a) Draw a simple diagram of the human excretory system and label the kidney, ureters, bladder and urethra. (b) Write two important functions of the kidney. (c) What is a nephron?
questions.answer: (a) Two bean-shaped kidneys in the upper abdomen near the back; a ureter from each runs down to the urinary bladder; the urethra leads out from the bladder. (b) Kidneys remove nitrogenous wastes (urea) from the blood as urine, and regulate the water and mineral balance of the body (osmoregulation). (c) A nephron is the structural and functional unit of the kidney — a Bowman's capsule with a glomerulus, where blood is filtered, and a tubule, where useful substances and water are reabsorbed, leaving urine.

questions.q: (a) Why is a balanced diet essential? Name the nutrients that must be part of it, with an example of each. (b) Deficiency of which nutrient causes anaemia, kwashiorkor and rickets? (c) Which nutrient will not be digested if the pancreas does not secrete lipase?
questions.answer: (a) A balanced diet gives energy, growth, repair and protection against disease. Nutrients: carbohydrates (rice, wheat), fats (ghee, oil), proteins (pulses, milk, eggs), vitamins (fruits, vegetables), minerals (green leafy vegetables, milk), water and roughage (raw vegetables). (b) Anaemia — iron; kwashiorkor — proteins; rickets — vitamin D (and calcium). (c) Fats, since lipase digests fats into fatty acids and glycerol.
